Research Methods requires at least 42 first-year EC, including Introduction to Political Science Research. The later research project requires Research Methods; this pathway completes it first.
Research project II: Practicing research skills
The International Relations core module requires at least 42 first-year EC. This example retains the specialisation selected from the primary programme page before UCR construction.

This example selects Sustainability Politics: Perspectives and Debates, 6 EC. It requires at least 42 first-year EC and cannot be combined with the alternative Violence and Security or European Union Politics module.

Beyond the Headlines is an eligible 6 EC seminar in the International Relations route. The 2026–2027 offering examines American politics and its international connections. Entry requires the full first year and at least 42 year-2 EC.

Democratic Backsliding is an eligible 12 EC seminar in the International Relations route. Entry requires the full first year and at least 42 year-2 EC; prior Democracies, Autocracies and Transitions is recommended.

The selected 12 EC thesis project is Contesting the Liberal International Order. Entry requires the full first year and at least 42 year-2 EC, including Research Methods. Completing both prior years meets the condition. The selected seminars and thesis are offered in the first semester; thirty EC remain open afterward.
Thirty EC remain open for approved elective or minor study within or outside Political Science, exchange or an optional placement. No particular minor, placement host or elective is assumed.
findings: The current public programme and dated 2026 catalogue agree on sixty EC per year. Retain International Relations as first-listed specialisation on the primary programme page; the guide lists other tracks in parallel and its aggregate year-three total includes their mutually exclusive groups. Only the eighteen seminar credits in the International Relations path, common twelve-credit thesis and thirty-credit open window are counted here.

The first-year ten courses total sixty. The year-two compulsory forty-two credits plus twelve-credit IR core module and six-credit Sustainability Politics total sixty. The dated course title is Sustainability Politics: Perspectives and Debates. Its forty-two first-year-credit entry rule is met; the excluded alternative Violence/Security and EU Politics modules are not added.

Research Methods requires at least forty-two first-year EC including Introduction to Political Science Research. Research Project II requires forty-two first-year EC and the year-two Research Methods course. The latter is taught in periods one and two before the period-three research-project offering. The remaining year-two core modules require forty-two first-year EC. Completing year one satisfies them; no minor- or exchange-only entry condition is imposed on regular degree students.

The IR study-path group expressly permits Beyond the Headlines, six EC in period one, and Democratic Backsliding, twelve EC in periods one and two. Both require the completed first year and forty-two year-two EC. The backsliding seminar recommends the earlier regimes course, which is completed. The thesis-project list permits Contesting the Liberal International Order, twelve EC in periods two and three; entry also requires Research Methods. All of years one and two are completed before these selections. Their thirty EC fit the first semester, leaving thirty open EC afterward.

The selected seminar investigates American politics and international links; the advanced seminar examines democratic erosion and its transnational dimensions. The thesis project supports individual IR research on contested global institutions. The core IR module surveys theoretical and empirical explanations of international politics rather than only conflict. Sustainability Politics examines institutions, inclusion, collective action and transitions. These underlying descriptions control bounded UCR correspondence.

The public programme preserves thirty open credits for elective/minor study inside or outside Political Science, exchange or optional placement. No specific open course, host or internship is instantiated. The chosen thesis and seminars have sufficient official curriculum and entry evidence, so an additional OER is not imposed as a redundant gate.
